gallery.title: File:French ambassador's residence - Washington, D.C..jpg
gallery.description: The French ambassador's residence is located at 2221 Kalorama Road NW in Washington, D.C.  Designed by Jules Henri de Sibour in 1910, the building is a combination of Tudor Revival and Jacobean Revival styles of architecture.  It is a contributing property to the Sheridan-Kalorama Historic District. Previous occupants include mining magnates William W. Lawrence and John Hays Hammond. The building served as the Embassy of France from 1936 until the current chancery was constructed at 4101 Reservoir Road NW.
categories: National Register of Historic Places with known IDs

gallery.title: File:4-9 Logan Circle NW Washington, D.C (cropped).jpg
gallery.description: Houses located at 4-9 Logan Circle NW in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C. They are contributing properties to the Logan Circle Historic District and Greater Fourteenth Street Historic District. From left to right: 4 Logan Circle was built around 1874. 5 Logan Circle was built in 1883 and designed by Emil S. Friedrich. 6 Logan Circle NW was built in 1878 and designed by Henry R. Searle. 7 Logan Circle NW was built in 1886 and designed by Robert Stead. 8 Logan Circle NW was built in 1885 and designed by Hornblower & Marshall. 9 Logan Circle NW was built in 1890 and designed by George P. Phelps.
